julia: Hey runtime team — getting multiple customer alerts about massive latency regressions on dedicated pool d-ed-12 starting ~03:10 UTC. Throughput per-GPU dropped ~4-6x, 95th latency jumped from 120ms -> 800ms. Can someone triage?
ken: On it. Do we have a correlation to autoscale events or a config change?
maria: I pulled metrics — autoscaler did one scale-down at 03:05 and then a scale-up at 03:12. But interestingly batcher metrics show queue_depth high while avg_batch_size collapsed to ~2 tokens per request. That smells like inefficient micro-batches from a tenant.
alex: Any noisy-tenant throttles firing? Also check max_batch_tokens and continuous-batcher window config for this pool.
maria: Logs snippet from the batcher node (node-7):
```
[03:08:55] batcher: enqueued req id=rt-9f3a low token_count=6 prefetched=false
[03:09:01] batcher: dispatched batch_size=2 total_tokens=18 latency_wait=52ms
[03:09:01] scheduler: selected kernel=fp16_q8 sequence_len=256
[03:09:02] inference: tokens/s=380
[03:11:12] batcher: queue_depth=122 microbatch_ratio=0.72 small_batch_ratio=0.81
[03:12:10] autoscaler: scale_up from 4->6 nodes reason=cpu>0.9
```
maria: Note microbatch_ratio = fraction of batches with <=4 requests. small_batch_ratio is very high.
ken: Could be a spike of many short-request clients (e.g., 1-2 token edits) hitting the pool. That increases per-token overhead, breaks batching effectiveness. Any tenant_id hotspots in logs?
julia: Support captured one customer request trace. They do lots of 1-3 token re-rank calls at high QPS. Repro curl attached: `curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TK>' -d '{"prompt":"a","max_tokens":2}'` run in a tight loop.
alex: If those are honest workload patterns, we should autoscale differently or enforce tenant-level QPS caps. Immediate mitigations: 1) increase max_batch_tokens for d-ed-12 from 8192->16384 to allow more packing, 2) relax continuous-batcher max_wait_ms from 25ms->50ms to give more time to pack, 3) enable prefix caching for that workload if repeat prefixes exist.
maria: Tried a quick canary: bumped max_batch_tokens on one node-group and increased max_wait_ms — avg batch_size rose from 2 -> 8 and tokens/s doubled on that group, 95th latency down to ~300ms. But overall pool still lagging because autoscaler removed two nodes earlier and pack imbalance persisted.
infra-bot: alert: high small-batch ratio detected on pool d-ed-12 (rule: small_batch_ratio>0.6 for 5m).
ken: Longer-term: scheduler should do tenant-aware packing and preemptive aggregation of tiny requests from same tenant to improve locality. Also consider per-tenant token-based shaping to avoid single tenant eating lots of slots with tiny requests.
julia: Support asked whether this is a billing/auth problem — we validated auth logs show no errors, it's pure throughput/packing inefficiency. Billing spike corresponds to more requests but token-util % low.
ops-bot: incident-log: escalated to eng-runtime on-call @ken @maria at 03:20 UTC.
alex: Action items I propose: 
- short: revert aggressive scale-down policy (increase min_nodes from 4->6) and temp raise max_wait_ms to 50ms for d-ed-12; enable tenant soft-QPS limit to 200r/s per tenant for 24h.
- medium: implement a small-batch detector that routes suspicious short-request flows to a separate packing queue with relaxed timeouts to avoid polluting main packer.
- long: add scheduler improvements for token-aware placement and tenant-aware packing.
maria: I'm running a 30m soak with the quick fixes on a canary subset now, will report metrics in 15m. So far pack efficiency improved.
ken: If soak looks good we'll roll to whole pool and coordinate with sales for impacted customers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
